This seminar report examines limits and colimits in category theory, building on Chapter~5 of Steve Awodey's \emph{Category Theory}. We first summarize the core theoretical framework, covering subobjects, pullbacks, general limits and colimits, their construction from products/coproducts and equalizers/coequalizers, and $\omega$-complete partial orders.
We then discuss concrete applications in computer science—including relational databases, algebraic data types, propositions as types, and computational category theory—followed by a summary of the seminar discussion and solutions to the assigned exercises in the appendix.
